Two parallel things must be kept apart. (1) VARIOLATION (the inoculation technique, the actual home-civ artefact): originated in Asia — China and/or India — with the only firmly documented early accounts being two from the mid-16th century, one Chinese and one Indian (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variolation; pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov "The origins of inoculation"). Chinese method = nasal insufflation (powdered smallpox scabs blown into the nostril), documented from a 1549 book and Needham's 1567-1572 window. Earlier Chinese dates circulated by Chinese-institutional sources — Tang 713-741 ("江南赵氏鼻苗种痘"), Song 998 CE (Wang Dan's son Wang Su) per zh.wikipedia.org/天花 and baike.baidu.com/人痘 — are explicitly legendary/poorly-documented and rejected by mainstream scholarship (PMC: implausible such a practice stayed secret ~500 yrs). India: scarification, ~16th-18th c.; the ancient-Sanskrit-origin claim is rejected (no prophylaxis described in the texts). AFRICA (West Africa/Sudan) had an INDEPENDENT variolation tradition: Onesimus taught Cotton Mather, driving the Boston 1721 trial in PARALLEL to the Ottoman route (who.int history-of-smallpox-vaccination; royalsociety.org). Ottoman Empire: variolation widely practised; Lady Mary Wortley Montagu observed it in Constantinople 1717, inoculated her son 1718 / daughter 1721 — the Ottoman-to-Britain leg. (2) VACCINATION (distinct, safer, cowpox): Edward Jenner, 1796, James Phipps. WHO eradication 1980. Home civs China/Ottoman/Britain all sit on the true spine; the under-credited non-home origins are India, sub-Saharan/West Africa, and (debatably) the broader 'Asia'.

ground_truth_origin:
Mechanical clock = bipolar-origin artefact; ground truth is a DISJUNCTION, not a point. (1) Chinese water-driven escapement strand: Zhang Heng (c.132 CE water-driven armillary), Yi Xing + Liang Lingzan (725 CE, first escapement releasing water-power in unit impulses), Zhang Sixun (976 CE), culminating in Su Song water-powered astronomical clock tower at Kaifeng 1088-1094 -- the earliest known timekeeper with an escapement; treatise Xinyi Xiangfayao survives 1092/1094. (2) European weight-driven all-mechanical strand: verge-and-foliot escapement c.1275; mechanical-clock references proliferate in church records 1280-1320; first fully mechanical weight-driven clocks in Western Europe (Italy/England/France/Germany) c.1300; oldest survivor Salisbury Cathedral 1386. CRUX: the two strands are technologically distinct (water-power + constant-force escapement vs weight-power + verge oscillator) and there is NO documented transmission China->Europe -- Needham speculated westward diffusion and called Su Song clock a direct ancestor, but mainstream scholarship treats the European weight-driven clock as plausibly-independent. Truthful where/when = China 8th-11th c. escapement/water-mechanical origin AND Europe c.1300 weight-driven all-mechanical, transmission unproven. Sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Su_Song; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_timekeeping_devices; ebsco.com First-Mechanical-Clock research-starter; kf.cn (Kaifeng, world clocks set out from Kaifeng); news.qq.com / chinanews.com.cn (Chinese-institutional framing of the water-powered armillary/clock as the direct ancestor of the world mechanical clock).</ground_truth_origin>

Telescope originates in the Netherlands (Middelburg, Zeeland) in 1608: Hans Lippershey filed the first patent application (2 Oct 1608) with the Dutch States General; near-simultaneous competing claims by Jacob Metius and Sacharias Janssen — no patent granted because the device was already widely known/easy to copy. Galileo (Padua/Venice, Italy) improved it (3x->23x) and was first to turn it systematically to the sky in 1609-1610 (Sidereus Nuncius). Later: Kepler (two-convex design, 1611), Newton (first reflector, 1668), Cassegrain (1672). Genuine NON-WESTERN precursor is the Islamic optical tradition — Ibn al-Haytham/Alhazen's Kitab al-Manazir (Book of Optics, c.1011-1021) and Ibn Sahl on refraction — plus European spectacles (late-13th-c. Italy) and reading stones; the disputed English Leonard Digges 'perspective glass' (mid-1500s) is evidentially weak. NO Chinese origin: even Chinese-institutional sources confirm Europe-origin and Jesuit transmission to China (Matteo Ricci ~1610; Adam Schall's Yuanjing shuo / 远镜说 introducing Galilean optics, 1626). Sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_telescope, britannica.com (Lippershey; Ibn al-Haytham), coema.org.cn (望远镜的历史), hsta.ustc.edu.cn (Macau Univ. CE → 1698 → 1712 → 1769/1781 → 19th-c. industrialization. Home civ = Greece/Britain. Diffused west via Mongol/Yuan era; Europe's first banknotes Stockholms Banco 1661. Seismoscope (the originating artefact): Zhang Heng (张衡), 132 CE, Han Dynasty China, capital Luoyang (Luoyang/Loyang) — the Houfeng Didong Yi (候风地动仪), a bronze urn ~2m wide with 8 dragon-heads/balls and an internal pendulum (du-zhu). It is a SEISMOSCOPE / 验震器 — it detects and indicates the direction of a distant quake; it does NOT continuously record motion and does NOT predict. The MODERN instrument is a separate, NON-Chinese lineage: first electromagnetic recording seismometer = Luigi Palmieri, Italy, 1855/56; first true recording seismograph ~ Filippo Cecchi, Italy, c.1875; first modern horizontal-pendulum seismograph = John Milne (with Ewing & Gray), Japan, 1880 — Milne is 'father of modern seismology'. So: China = origin of the detection device; Italy + Japan/Europe = origin of the modern instrument; there is no demonstrated direct China→modern technical descent. Sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seismometer, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Milne (EN); baike.baidu.com, china-csm.org (Chinese Society for Measurement), kepu.gov.cn (China official sci-pop portal), zh.wikipedia.org, news.sjtu.edu.cn, jiemian.com (CN-institutional). The CN sources themselves carry a self-critical strand: Feng Rui / China Earthquake Administration (2003) and SJTU note it is a seismoscope and that Wang Zhenduo's famous 1951 reconstruction was mechanically flawed and the textbook model was withdrawn.

True paper = sheets of macerated/pulped plant-cellulose fibre (hemp, ramie, mulberry bast), categorically distinct from Egyptian papyrus (laminated reed strips, not pulped — NOT true paper). ORIGIN: China. Archaeological fragments push it to the Western Han, 2nd c. BCE — over a century before Cai Lun: Fangmatan (Gansu, c.179–141 BCE, ink map), Baqiao (Xi'an, 2nd c. BCE), and 460+ fragments at the Xuanquanzhi/Dunhuang relay station (1st c. BCE–1st c. CE). Cai Lun (105 CE) IMPROVED/systematised (cheaper mulberry-bast + rags + fishing-net pulp), he did not invent it. Spread: Islamic world (Samarkand 8th c., Baghdad 793 CE; Talas 751 CE story disputed) → Europe (Xàtiva/Iberia 1056, Fabriano Italy 13th c.) → wood-pulp industrialisation (Fourdrinier 1799, mechanical wood pulp 1840s). Key Chinese-institutional nuance: China's own scholars do NOT uniformly inflate the earliest claim — the China National Pulp & Paper Research Institute argued Baqiao is waste-hemp padding (not paper) and the Fangmatan 'map' is likely textile; Guo Weitao & Ma Xiaowen (China Daily WAC 2023) argue the early graph 纸 denoted silk/textile, so the reliably science-dated plant-fibre papers are Jianshui Jinguan, Zhongyan, Maquanwan, Yumenguan — still mid/late Western Han (1st c. BCE). Sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_paper, silkroads.org.cn, chinadaily.com.cn (WAC 2023 Guo & Ma), britannica.com (Fangmatan), gmw.cn.

ground_truth_origin: Magnetic compass: origin = CHINA, unanimous and well-grounded. Multilingual harvest (en.wikipedia History_of_the_compass; zh.wikipedia 指南针; baike.baidu.com; sohu.com/bjd.com.cn on Wang Zhenduo; qulishi.com) converges: (a) lodestone-attracts-iron known in Warring States (~4th c. BCE, Guiguzi/Hanfeizi); (b) the 'Sinan' (司南) south-pointing spoon is referenced in Han-era Lunheng (Wang Chong, c.70-80 CE) as a DIVINATION tool — NOT navigation; (c) the true functional compass = magnetized needle, first described by Shen Kuo, Dream Pool Essays / Mengxi Bitan, 1088 CE (incl. magnetic declination); (d) first NAVIGATION reference = Zhu Yu, Pingzhou Ketan, 1111-1119 CE (events ~1086). Transmission: Europe ~1180-1190 (Alexander Neckam, De naturis rerum); Persian/Arab references 1232 (Jawami ul-Hikayat) and 1282 (Baylak al-Qibjaqi). Consensus (Kreutz/Needham): Chinese navigational use predates first European mention by ~150 yrs; European route (independent vs via Arab intermediaries) genuinely debated. KEY NUANCE the harvest surfaces — and notably CHINESE-INSTITUTIONAL sources flag it loudest: the '2nd c. BCE working compass' claim is CONTESTED. No Han magnetic-spoon artifact has ever been excavated; Wang Zhenduo's 1940s reconstruction only partially worked and Qian Linzhao's 1950s replication FAILED (natural lodestone too weak to beat spoon/plate friction); a 'Big Dipper / 斗杓' counter-reading (Liu Bingzheng 1956, Sun Ji 2005) disputes whether Sinan was magnetic at all. So the defensible hard dates are 1088 (needle) and 1111-19 (navigation); the '~200 BCE' figure is a soft, divination-only, physically-unverified claim.

ground_truth_origin: Origin = Hellenistic Greek world (Alexandria). The planispheric astrolabe is solidly documented only in late antiquity: Theon of Alexandria wrote a treatise (c. 4th c. Islamic refinement is real and central: Muhammad al-Fazari (d. ~796) first built one in Islam; al-Sufi (10th c.) documented 1000+ uses; earliest SURVIVING instrument is AH 315 = 927-928 CE; qibla-direction and prayer-time functions are genuinely Islamic innovations. ground_truth_origin: Artefact = distillation. Real origin is a multi-stage lineage, NOT a single point. (1) Earliest physical apparatus: Tepe Gawra, northern Mesopotamia/Iraq, Late Chalcolithic c. 4200-3500 BCE, terracotta retorts for aromatic essences/perfume — but "true distillation" here is contested (Levey 1950/1973 hypothesis; EXARC experimental-archaeology reappraisal). Written record: Babylonian cuneiform tablet of Tapputi c. 1200 BCE (perfumery; "distillation vs decoction" debated). (exarc.net, ancient-origins.net). (2) The decisive apparatus + theory — the alembic/ambix proper, tribikos, kerotakis, bain-marie — Hellenistic Alexandria 1st-3rd c. CE, Maria the Jewess, documented by Zosimos of Panopolis c.300 CE (the "Hellenistic" home pole). (3) Distillation of ALCOHOL and systematic refinement: Islamic Golden Age — al-Kindi (d.873, Kitab... fi al-itr), Jabir ibn Hayyan, al-Razi (Kitab al-Asrar); the word "alembic" = Arabic al- + Greek ambix (the "Islamic" home pole). (history-science-technology.com, 1001inventions.com, muslimheritage.com). (4) Independent/parallel weak-alcohol stills: India/Gandhara-Taxila c.150 BCE-350 CE (Allchin) — but the "Gandhara still" was challenged 2024-25 as non-functional (Antiquity/Cambridge; Springer s12520-025-02301-8). (5) China: distilled liquor with a strong NATIVE-origin claim (Jin/Song dynasty; archaeological stills Qinglong 1975, Acheng 2006); the older "araki<Arabic, arrived Yuan dynasty via Mongols" theory is now contested in Chinese scholarship as actually Jurchen (sohu.com/a/456169437, guancha; Li Shizhen Bencao Gangmu "shaojiu...zi Yuan shi shichuang"). Home civ Hellenistic/Islamic is correctly the hinge of the canonical Western lineage; Mesopotamia is the proto-origin upstream of it.
